findings.text: VFS exposes a set operation for file attributes that authorizes the caller, validates proposed values against current values, consults encryption and security policy, then delegates persistence to the owning filesystem and emits change notification on success.

User access to classic flags, extended filesystem attributes and generic file attribute objects is provided through ioctl and fd-or-path system entry points that translate between user and kernel representations and hold mount write protection across mutation.

Transitions of append-only and immutable state require a dedicated immutable capability, and encryption policy is consulted before any other project or extent validation; failure at either gate aborts the update with an error.

Project identifier and project-inherit state may only change inside the initial user namespace, with out-of-namespace attempts rejected; inside that namespace a changed identifier must satisfy kernel project validity.

Extent size hints and copy and direct-access hints are restricted by object type, with plain extents for regular files, inheritance hint for directories, copy hint for files or directories, and direct-access hint for files or directories; zero sizes implicitly clear their corresponding enablement.

When the caller supplies only one attribute family, the other family members are carried over from current values, preserving filesystem-specific extended properties when classic flags are supplied and preserving classic properties when extended properties are supplied.

File attribute system calls accept only nofollow and empty-path options, follow symlinks unless nofollow is given, reject oversized or undersized user buffers, support fd-based operation when no pathname is supplied, and normalize unsupported-operation errors to a common not-supported result.
Attribute read-modify-validate-commit is serialized by exclusive inode ownership held across retrieval of old values, preparation, security check and filesystem commit, always released before return.

Sysctl tree creation, insertion, lookup and reference dropping require holding the global sysctl spin protection, with unregister temporarily releasing it while waiting for active users; sibling dcache invalidation combines RCU traversal with per-inode grabbing and superblock activation.

A backing file object embeds a full file object plus a union that holds either a user path or a release callback, with an additional opaque security pointer present when security support is enabled and retrievable through a dedicated accessor.

System-wide file accounting combines a small statistics record holding current and maximum counts with separate slab caches for normal and backing files and a cacheline-aligned per-CPU live-file counter.

Sysctl registration state consists of headers that reference a table slice and per-entry red-black nodes, directories that anchor a red-black root, and a table-entry iterator that walks the slice by index; headers track use counts, registration counts and unregister state plus parent and set links.

Sysctl table lifetime moves from allocation and initialization through validation, directory creation and ordered entry insertion to reference-counted teardown where last drop triggers unlinking, user drain, dcache purge, tree removal and deferred reclamation with recursive parent release.

File attribute mutation follows acquire-write-protection then VFS set then release protection, with mount syscalls using mount-based hold and ioctl paths using file-based hold that pairs superblock write start with mount access acquisition and reverses both on completion or failure.

Boot initialization publishes filesystem file accounting under the fs sysctl namespace and optionally reserves a mount point for binary-format handling, computing the live file count on demand from the per-CPU counter.

Inserting a duplicate proc name within a directory fails and logs the conflicting directory path and name, and permanently-empty directory semantics reject normal insertion with read-only failure and reject promotion of a non-empty directory to permanently empty.

Unregister must wait for concurrent users to drain before removing tree links because lookup walks header lists, and must purge proc dentries for the removed headers since namespaced duplicates can otherwise contaminate the dcache.
Filesystem statistics are exposed as file-nr read-only, file-max read-write bounded below by zero, and nr_open read-write bounded by dedicated minimum and maximum controls.
File attribute system calls enforce a minimum version-zero object size and a page-sized maximum, rejecting flag combinations outside the supported nofollow and empty-path set.

File-based mount write acquisition starts superblock write protection before requesting mount write access and undoes the superblock protection if mount acquisition fails; release always undoes mount access before ending superblock protection.

Non-initial sysctl sets maintain placeholder link entries in the core tree that point back to their owning root, created by translating the target directory across sets and only when every table entry lacks a suitable existing link or directory.
